name: renders the full hierarchy and emits skip-level pairs
input: R manages S and T; S manages V; T manages U
test:
relations = [['R', 'S', 'T'], ['S', 'V'], ['T', 'U']]
children, root = build_children(relations)
assert root == 'R'
assert children == {'R': ['S', 'T'], 'S': ['V'], 'T': ['U'], 'V': [], 'U': []}
assert render_full_chain(relations) == 'R\n....S\n........V\n....T\n........U'
assert all_skip_level_pairs(relations) == [('R', 'V'), ('R', 'U')]

name: selected chain prints the target once and preserves sibling order
input: CEO tree with a deeper ML subtree
test:
relations = [['CEO', 'Eng', 'Sales'], ['Eng', 'Infra', 'ML'], ['ML', 'Search']]
assert render_full_chain(relations) == 'CEO
....Eng
........Infra
........ML
............Search
....Sales'
assert render_chain_for(relations, 'ML') == 'CEO
....Eng
........ML
............Search'
assert all_skip_level_pairs(relations) == [('CEO', 'Infra'), ('CEO', 'ML'), ('Eng', 'Search')]
assert lowest_common_manager(relations, 'Infra', 'Search') == 'Eng'
assert lowest_common_manager(relations, 'Search', 'Sales') == 'CEO'
